article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant autoflowering hybrid
Genetics: Master Kush × Ruderalis
Breeder: Dutch Passion
THC Content: Moderate to high
CBD Content: Not officially specified
Terpene Profile: myrcene , limonene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Sweet earth, citrus, Kush spice, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60–70 days from seed to harvest
Outdoor Harvest Time: 9–10 weeks after germination
Indoor Yield: 25–50 g per plant
Outdoor Yield: 25–50 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy

Snowstorm comes from the early era of autoflowering cannabis , when breeders were still proving that ruderalis genetics could produce more than tiny plants with mild effects. Dutch Passion chose one of its established Afghan varieties, Master Kush, and combined it with a carefully selected autoflowering ruderalis line. The objective was straightforward but technically demanding: preserve the compact strength, sweet-earthy flavor, resin production, and relaxing character of Kush while adding the ability to flower automatically according to age. The breeding project reportedly required almost two years before Dutch Passion considered the line stable enough for release.

The finished cultivar took its name from its appearance near harvest. Dense green flowers become coated with pale resin until the plant can resemble a small Christmas tree covered by fresh snow. At only about 30–70 centimeters in the breeder’s original specifications, Snowstorm was designed for growers who wanted marijuana that stayed compact, finished rapidly, and did not require a seasonal change in daylight. Importantly, the strain covered here is the original Master Kush × Ruderalis Snowstorm. Dutch Passion later released SnowStorm #2 using Orange Bud × Ruderalis genetics, making the two related in concept but genetically distinct cultivars.
Genetics and Lineage

The original Snowstorm is Master Kush × Ruderalis. Dutch Passion selected its Master Kush as the THC-rich parent, describing this cannabis strain as a sturdy Afghan indica originating from the Hindu Kush region. The breeder’s modern Master Kush remains a compact, resilient marijuana plant valued for heavy flowers, an approximately eight-week photoperiod bloom, earthy-citrus flavor, and deeply relaxing Kush effects. Those qualities provided a strong foundation for an early autoflower project because the plant already possessed much of the compact structure breeders wanted to preserve.

Ruderalis contributes an entirely different feature: age-dependent flowering. Conventional photoperiod cannabis begins flowering in response to longer uninterrupted darkness, but autoflower genetics can initiate reproduction largely according to plant maturity. Dutch Passion spent nearly two years working this trait into the Master Kush background while selecting for potency, resin production, stability, and manageable structure. The original breeder description ultimately characterized Snowstorm as a stable, resin-rich indica-ruderalis cultivar capable of completing its entire lifecycle in roughly 60–70 days.

Confusion developed after Dutch Passion introduced SnowStorm #2. That later plant was not simply a revised Master Kush phenotype. Dutch Passion identifies SnowStorm #2 as Orange Bud × Ruderalis and describes it as an automatic version of its classic Orange Bud Skunk line. Anyone researching original Snowstorm genetics should therefore check whether a source is discussing the Master Kush cultivar or its Orange Bud-based successor.
Effects and Experience

Snowstorm’s experience reflects the Kush side more strongly than the ruderalis contribution. The beginning can bring a pleasant mental shift without the aggressive cerebral acceleration associated with Haze or tropical sativas. Mood becomes lighter, external distractions lose some importance, and the overall pace of the experience tends to feel comfortable rather than urgent. Sweet Kush-derived cannabis of this type can suit music, relaxed conversation, movies, or quiet recreational activities where stimulation is welcome but productivity is not the primary goal.

Physical relaxation becomes more prominent as the session develops. The body can feel heavier, muscles loosen, and the desire to remain highly active often declines. Dutch Passion’s description of the Master Kush parent emphasizes soothing, calming effects, and that underlying character carries naturally into the original Snowstorm breeding concept. Larger servings are consequently more appropriate for late afternoon or evening than circumstances requiring precise coordination.

Exact potency is difficult to state responsibly. The original cultivar came from an era when breeders rarely attached a standardized laboratory THC percentage to every seed release, and Dutch Passion’s historical Snowstorm specifications do not provide one. Descriptions of “astonishing potency” should therefore be understood relative to early autoflowering cannabis, which was often significantly weaker than today’s best automatic varieties.
Medical Benefits

Snowstorm has not undergone controlled clinical trials as an individual medical marijuana cultivar. Its possible appeal to medical cannabis consumers comes instead from its predominantly relaxing THC-oriented experience. Some consumers may prefer this type of weed when seeking temporary relief from stress, everyday muscular tension, or difficulty mentally disengaging after an active day.

The cultivar’s Kush-like body relaxation may also make it more appropriate for evening use than highly stimulating sativa strains . Appetite can increase as the effects settle, and higher doses may become sleepy. Those observations should not be interpreted as evidence that Snowstorm treats pain, insomnia, anxiety, or any other medical condition.

THC responses differ substantially between individuals. Dry mouth, dizziness, anxiety, impaired coordination, and excessive sedation remain possible, particularly with stronger flower or larger doses. Anyone using cannabis medically should rely on the laboratory analysis of the actual product and qualified healthcare guidance instead of assuming that every plant carrying the Snowstorm name has identical cannabinoid chemistry.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweet earth and citrus form the core of the original Snowstorm profile. Dutch Passion specifically selected Master Kush partly because of its smooth smoke and sweet, earthy-citrus character, qualities the breeder stated were retained in the autoflowering offspring. The result is much closer to traditional Afghan Kush than to the intensely fruity autoflowers developed in later generations.

Breaking apart mature flowers can release dry soil, herbs, citrus peel, mild spice, and a deeper resinous aroma. Sweetness often becomes more noticeable during consumption, while earthy Kush characteristics linger after the brighter citrus notes fade. Some plants may lean more herbal or peppery depending on phenotype and growing conditions.

No authoritative terpene laboratory panel survives for the original Dutch Passion release. Myrcene, limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and pinene would be chemically plausible contributors to an earthy, citrus, spicy, and herbal profile, but assigning a universal dominant terpene would go beyond the available evidence. Individual laboratory testing is the only dependable method of determining a specific batch’s terpene composition.
Growing Information

Compact dimensions were one of Snowstorm’s strongest selling points. Dutch Passion’s original specifications placed plants at approximately 30–70 centimeters, making the cultivar suitable for restricted vertical spaces and small outdoor gardens. The complete lifecycle was listed at roughly 60–70 days, with flowering beginning automatically rather than after a grower changed the light schedule. That simplicity made the strain particularly accessible to people experimenting with autoflowering marijuana for the first time.

Historical production was approximately 25–50 grams per plant. Those numbers may look modest beside modern autoflowers, but they reflect the stage of automatic breeding at the time. The important achievement was combining reasonable flower quality with compact dimensions, feminized seeds, rapid maturation, and dependable autoflowering behavior. Master Kush also contributed a forgiving constitution and the ability to grow in soil, coco, or hydroponic environments.

Autoflowers have little time to recover from severe stress because their internal flowering clock continues regardless of plant size. Snowstorm therefore benefits from a smooth early life rather than aggressive pruning or repeated transplantation. Its compact stature makes elaborate training unnecessary in most situations. Outdoors, growers are not tied to an October harvest; plants started during suitable weather can theoretically mature roughly nine to ten weeks later, allowing cultivation to coincide with the strongest period of available sunlight.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Snowstorm?
The original Dutch Passion Snowstorm is Master Kush × Ruderalis. Dutch Passion used its Afghan Master Kush as the THC-rich parent and crossed it with a selected autoflowering ruderalis line.
Is Snowstorm an autoflower strain?

Yes. Snowstorm was part of Dutch Passion’s early AutoFem breeding program. It flowers automatically and completes its full lifecycle in approximately 60–70 days rather than requiring a 12/12 flowering light schedule.
Is Snowstorm the same as SnowStorm #2?

No. The original Snowstorm is Master Kush × Ruderalis. SnowStorm #2 was a later Dutch Passion cultivar based on Orange Bud × Ruderalis and was developed as an autoflowering version of Orange Bud. Dutch Passion now lists SnowStorm #2 as discontinued.
What does Snowstorm weed taste like?

The original strain leans toward sweet earth, citrus, herbs, and Kush spice. These characteristics were inherited primarily from the Master Kush parent, which Dutch Passion describes as earthy, citrus-dominant, sweet, and spicy.
How long does Snowstorm take from seed to harvest?

Dutch Passion’s historical specifications place the full lifecycle at approximately 60–70 days, or roughly nine to ten weeks from germination. Plants typically remain compact at about 30–70 centimeters.
Final Thoughts on Snowstorm

Snowstorm is more interesting as a piece of autoflowering cannabis history than its modest yield figures might initially suggest. Dutch Passion took an established Afghan Master Kush and spent almost two years incorporating automatic flowering while trying to preserve the parent’s potency, resin, stability, and sweet earthy-citrus character. The finished plant could remain under a meter tall and move from seed to mature marijuana flower in around two months—qualities that were still relatively novel when early AutoFem genetics entered the market.

Modern autoflowers can grow larger, yield far more, and reach cannabinoid levels that would have seemed exceptional during Snowstorm’s era. Yet those advances were built on breeding projects like this one. The original Master Kush × Ruderalis Snowstorm helped demonstrate that automatic cannabis could carry recognizable genetics from an established photoperiod strain rather than existing merely as weak ruderalis-dominant weed. Its later replacement, Orange Bud-based SnowStorm #2, shows how quickly Dutch Passion continued refining the concept. For growers and enthusiasts interested in the evolution of autoflower marijuana, the original Snowstorm remains an instructive early step between primitive automatic varieties and the high-performance autos available today.
